INSO:s övergripande målsättning är att: 1. Lindra nöd för människor som drabbas av konflikter, naturkatastrofer eller andra krissituationer. 2. Säkerställa biståndsarbetares välbefinnande och säkerhet. Dessa mål ämnas uppnås genom att: 1. Tillhandahålla säkerhetstjänster till humanitära organisationer som arbetar för att lindra nöd och rädda liv. 2. Främja och underlätta en bredare förståelse av konflikter och dess inverkan på humanitär säkerhet och global, regional och lokal utveckling.

title.narrative: 2 Amendment to the Agreement on Core Support between Sida and Stichting International NGO Safety Organisation, INSO , (16975)
Grant Agreement between The Swedish International Cooperation Agency Sida and Stitching International NGO Safety Organisation, INSO regarding Core support
Beslut om ändring av insats, INSO International NGO Safety Organisation 2024-2025 (16975)

description.narrative:
In 2024, INSO delivered results against the 3 output areas presented in its log-frame and approved by Sida, in support of 1351 NGO partners across 19 countries:
Output 1: Scalable, relevant and adaptive safety and access platforms. Output 2: Expanded outreach and use of CHDC by humanitarian responders. Output 3: Field driven advocacy, research and engagement.
All set targets were met, and most of the time exceeded. Overachievement, where observed, is an encouraging sign, but INSO also recognizes the importance of ensuring that targets remain realistic and aligned with both our operational capacity and the evolving context.
Among the results: - INSO successfully piloted the deployment of an emergency response team to Lebanon, on the onset of the crisis. The learning was incorporated into INSOs approach to emergency response programming. - INSOs Digital Learning team launched the INSO NGO Security Management online course on the DisasterReady platform for all humanitarian workers. - Also during 2024 a new country office was established in Chad and INSO relaunched the CHDC (Conflict and Humanitarian Data center) which successfully brought 30 partners on board, with high level of satisfaction from participants. - INSO roving training team provided a range of trainings (security management, humanitarian negotiation,) to 289 participants in 3 countries. National NGO participants represented 26% of all participants. - Overall, efforts were made to remove barriers to national NGO participation, which increased from 10% in 2023, to 15% in 2024. Women represented 33% of all participants. This follows efforts made since the release of a gender memo by INSO in 2022 after which the organisation has seen a clear and immediate positive impact on female participation, rising from 20% in 2022, to 24% in 2023, 31% in 2024, and 32% in the first half of 2025.
Additionally, during the fourth quarter of 2024, INSO's in-country training teams delivered 111 sessions for 1,370 participants. `
Finally, to mark World Humanitarian Day, INSO issued a report identifying emerging dynamics, including an upward trend in serious NGO incidents, growing government involvement in NGO risk, rising instrumentalisation of aid, and concerns around mis/disinformation.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
